Lessons.Title: Assess the Reasonableness of Solutions
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will solve multi-step word problems by analyzing data, estimating, reasoning, and performing multiple operations.
In the final lesson of the unit, you apply your knowledge of numbers in base-ten and your estimation and computation skills to solve problems about languages and populations in the United States.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Native American Languages (10 minutes); Activity 1: Do You Speak Navajo? (20 minutes); Activity 2: Languages in Philadelphia and Chicago (15 minutes); Cool-down: The Children and the Elderly (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Read actual axes, category labels, table values and units before estimating and computing multi-step differences.

Edulytics authored model: Identify the relevant source bar/table data before calculating. Estimate a difference using rounded values, then subtract the actual numbers. First-party arithmetic model: 7,025 − 3,981 = 3,044; estimate 7,000 − 4,000 = 3,000.
First-party Cool-down: Given counts 7,025 and 3,981, estimate then calculate the difference.
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
